page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of a dedicated Intel Xeon 6455B processor operating at a high clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r7iz.16xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance. It achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in Passmark database operations and text processing. The Intel Xeon processor's support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions enables strong performance in specialized workloads, including medium-model LLM inference prompt processing and cryptographic operations. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, with large-block read operations reaching 244.57 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7iz.16xlarge offers a high-performance profile for memory-intensive workloads without the added expense of GPU hardware. However, the complete absence of local NVMe storage represents a key tradeoff, requiring reliance on network-attached storage for all disk operations. This configuration is highly suited for memory-bound and compute-heavy applications such as relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
